The invention relates to a method and system for delivering ordered items by using delivery containers that are loaded onto transport racks. The system is designed to support the efficient handling, transport, temporary storage, and final collection of items that have been ordered by consignees.

According to the method, items are first picked at a supply depot in accordance with orders that have been placed. Each order, or part of an order, is placed into a corresponding delivery container. The delivery containers therefore serve as transport units for the ordered items and allow the items to be handled in an organized and traceable manner throughout the delivery process.

A computer system is used to determine the sequence in which the delivery containers are to be loaded onto a transport rack. This loading sequence may be based on various factors, such as the intended destination of each container, the planned route of the transport rack, the order in which containers will be unloaded, or the collection times assigned to the consignees. By determining the loading sequence in advance, the system can improve handling efficiency and reduce unnecessary rearrangement of containers during transport and unloading.

Once the delivery containers have been loaded onto the transport rack in the determined sequence, the transport rack is moved from the supply depot to a buffer depot or collection depot by a transport system. The transport system may include, for example, a vehicle, conveyor system, automated guided vehicle, or another suitable means for transferring the loaded rack between locations.

At the buffer or collection depot, the delivery containers are handled according to the intended collection process. In one option, the containers are placed into storage compartments, where they remain until they are collected or further processed. These compartments may be assigned to individual orders, consignees, or collection time slots. In another option, a delivery container is moved directly to a service location, where the consignee can collect the ordered items.

Overall, the invention provides an organized delivery system in which ordered items are picked into delivery containers, the containers are loaded onto transport racks in a computer-determined sequence, and the loaded racks are transported to a depot where the containers are either stored or made available for collection. This arrangement can improve the efficiency, reliability, and traceability of order delivery and collection operations.
outputs.L4:
A delivery method and system are provided for supplying goods from a supply depot to a buffer depot, where the goods can later be collected by a consignee on demand. The method begins at the supply depot, where individual items ordered for delivery are picked and placed into delivery containers. Each delivery container may be assigned to a particular consignee, order, destination, or collection request, and the contents of the container may be recorded in a computer system so that the location and status of the order can be tracked throughout the process.

After the items have been order-picked into the delivery containers, the containers are loaded onto transport racks. The loading sequence is determined by a computer system, which may take into account factors such as delivery priority, destination, expected collection time, container size, routing requirements, or the order in which containers will be unloaded at the buffer depot. By loading the containers in a planned sequence, handling effort is reduced and the later transfer of containers at the buffer depot can be carried out more efficiently.

The transport racks are then moved from the supply depot to the buffer depot. The buffer depot may be located closer to the consignee than the supply depot and may function as an intermediate distribution point or collection station. Upon arrival at the buffer depot, each transport rack is positioned at or near a docking apparatus. The docking apparatus is configured to receive the transport rack and to interface with an automated storage and retrieval unit. This allows delivery containers to be transferred from the rack without requiring extensive manual handling.

At the buffer depot, the storage and retrieval unit automatically removes containers from the transport rack and determines, based on information from the control system, whether each container should be placed into temporary storage or moved directly to an issuing station. If the consignee has not yet arrived or has not yet requested collection, the container may be stored in an assigned storage location within the buffer depot. The storage location is recorded so that the container can be retrieved quickly when needed. If the consignee is already present or has submitted a collection request, the container may be conveyed directly to the issuing station.

When the consignee requests pickup, the system identifies the corresponding delivery container and instructs the storage and retrieval unit to retrieve it from storage. The container is then transported automatically to the issuing station, where it can be handed over to the consignee or made available through a secured collection interface. The issuing station may include identification, authentication, or confirmation features to ensure that the correct container is issued to the correct consignee.

This arrangement enables an efficient, request-based delivery and pickup process. Because containers are pre-picked at the supply depot, loaded onto transport racks in a computer-optimized sequence, and automatically handled at the buffer depot, the system reduces manual sorting, minimizes waiting times, and improves the reliability of order fulfillment. The buffer depot serves as a flexible intermediate storage and issuing location, allowing consignees to collect ordered items at convenient times while maintaining automated control over container movement, storage, retrieval, and delivery.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a European patent-style description of a method and system for delivering ordered goods from a supply depot to a collection depot, including reference numbers for components such as items (4), containers (3), computer system (2), transport rack (12), docking apparatus (54), and issuing station (56).
counterfactuals.output:
## Description

### Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a method and a system for delivering ordered goods from a supply depot to a collection depot. In particular, the invention relates to the preparation, transport, docking and issue of ordered items to a customer at a remote or local collection depot, wherein the items are accommodated in containers and are managed by a computer system.

### Background of the Invention

It is known to provide home delivery services or customer collection services for goods ordered remotely, for example via an online ordering platform. In such arrangements, goods are picked at a warehouse or store and are subsequently transported to the customer or made available for collection. Existing systems may require a high degree of manual handling at the collection location, may not provide reliable tracking of individual orders, and may be inefficient where a plurality of orders are transported together.

There is therefore a need for an improved method and system by which ordered goods can be prepared at a supply depot, transported efficiently to a collection depot, and issued to a customer in a controlled and traceable manner.

### Summary of the Invention

According to one aspect, there is provided a method of delivering ordered goods from a supply depot to a collection depot, the method comprising receiving, by a computer system (2), order data relating to one or more items (4) ordered by a customer, assigning at least one container (3) to the order, placing the ordered items (4) in the assigned container (3) at the supply depot, loading the container (3) onto a transport rack (12), transporting the transport rack (12) to the collection depot, coupling the transport rack (12) to a docking apparatus (54) at the collection depot, and issuing the container (3), or the items (4) contained therein, to the customer through an issuing station (56).

According to another aspect, there is provided a system for delivering ordered goods, the system comprising a computer system (2) configured to receive and process customer order data, a plurality of containers (3) each configured to receive one or more ordered items (4), at least one transport rack (12) configured to support a plurality of containers (3) during transport from a supply depot to a collection depot, a docking apparatus (54) arranged at the collection depot for receiving or coupling to the transport rack (12), and an issuing station (56) configured to permit authorised issue of the ordered items (4) to the customer.

The invention enables a plurality of customer orders to be assembled at a supply depot, transported in a structured manner, and issued at a collection depot with reduced manual handling. The use of the computer system (2) allows tracking of the containers (3), the items (4), and customer collection events.

### Brief Description of the Drawings

Embodiments of the invention will now be described by way of example with reference to the accompanying drawings, in which:

- **Figure 1** schematically shows a system for delivering ordered goods from a supply depot to a collection depot;
- **Figure 2** schematically shows containers (3) loaded with items (4);
- **Figure 3** schematically shows a transport rack (12) for receiving a plurality of containers (3);
- **Figure 4** schematically shows a docking apparatus (54) at a collection depot; and
- **Figure 5** schematically shows an issuing station (56) for issuing ordered goods to a customer.

### Detailed Description of Embodiments

Referring to Figure 1, a delivery system comprises a computer system (2), a plurality of containers (3), items (4) to be delivered, one or more transport racks (12), a docking apparatus (54), and an issuing station (56). The system is arranged to facilitate delivery of ordered goods from a supply depot, such as a warehouse, fulfilment centre, supermarket, store or distribution depot, to a collection depot, such as a customer collection point, automated collection station, retail outlet, vehicle loading point or local delivery hub.

The computer system (2) may comprise one or more servers, databases, terminals, mobile devices, scanners, controllers or networked computing devices. The computer system (2) is configured to receive order data representing an order placed by a customer. The order data may identify the customer, the ordered items (4), a preferred collection depot, a collection time window, payment status, and any storage conditions required for the items (4).

The items (4) may include grocery products, parcels, chilled goods, frozen goods, ambient goods, pharmaceuticals, prepared meals, retail products or any combination thereof. The items (4) are picked at the supply depot in response to instructions generated by the computer system (2). The computer system (2) may generate a picking list and may associate the ordered items (4) with one or more containers (3).

Each container (3) is preferably provided with an identification element, such as a barcode, QR code, RFID tag, electronic label or other machine-readable identifier. The identification element enables the computer system (2) to associate the container (3) with a particular customer order. A single customer order may be assigned to one container (3) or to a plurality of containers (3), for example where different temperature zones are required.

The containers (3) may be insulated, open, closed, lockable, stackable, reusable or disposable. In one embodiment, at least some of the containers (3) are temperature-controlled or are configured to maintain a temperature condition for the items (4) during transport. The containers (3) may include lids, handles, locking elements, location features or engagement formations for securing the containers (3) to the transport rack (12).

After the ordered items (4) have been placed in the assigned container (3), the container (3) is loaded onto a transport rack (12). The transport rack (12) may comprise a wheeled frame having a plurality of shelves, compartments, guides or support positions for receiving the containers (3). Each support position may have a respective location identifier, enabling the computer system (2) to record the position of each container (3) on the transport rack (12).

The transport rack (12) may be provided with a rack identifier, such as an RFID tag or barcode, and may be scanned or otherwise registered with the computer system (2) before departure from the supply depot. The computer system (2) may store data indicating which containers (3) and which orders are located on each transport rack (12). The transport rack (12) is then transported to the selected collection depot by a vehicle or other transport means.

At the collection depot, the transport rack (12) is received by or coupled to the docking apparatus (54). The docking apparatus (54) may comprise a mechanical receiving structure, an alignment guide, a locking device, an electrical connector, a data connector, a sensor, a scanner, a temperature-control interface or any combination thereof. In one embodiment, the docking apparatus (54) is configured to hold the transport rack (12) in a defined position relative to the issuing station (56).

The docking apparatus (54) may identify the transport rack (12) automatically, for example by reading the rack identifier. Alternatively, an operator may input or scan the identity of the transport rack (12). The docking apparatus (54) communicates, directly or indirectly, with the computer system (2) to confirm that the transport rack (12) has arrived at the correct collection depot. The computer system (2) may then update the status of each order associated with containers (3) on the transport rack (12) to indicate that the order is available for collection.

The issuing station (56) is arranged to issue the ordered items (4) to a customer. The issuing station (56) may comprise a user interface, display screen, keypad, card reader, code reader, biometric reader, communication module, door, hatch, conveyor, lift mechanism, robotic handling device, locking device or manual access point. The issuing station (56) may be located adjacent to or integrated with the docking apparatus (54).

To collect an order, the customer provides authorisation information at the issuing station (56). The authorisation information may comprise a personal identification number, collection code, payment card, mobile device credential, biometric identifier or other authentication data. The issuing station (56) transmits the authorisation information to the computer system (2), which verifies the customer and identifies the container or containers (3) associated with the order.

Following successful verification, the issuing station (56) enables access to the appropriate container (3) or causes the container (3) to be presented to the customer. In a manual embodiment, the issuing station (56) may indicate to an operator which container (3) is to be removed from the transport rack (12). In an automated embodiment, a handling mechanism may retrieve the container (3) from the transport rack (12) and present it at a customer-accessible opening of the issuing station (56).

The computer system (2) may record the issue of the container (3) or items (4), including the time of collection and the identity of the collecting customer or authorised representative. The status of the order may be updated to “collected”. If a container (3) is reusable, the issuing station (56) may require the customer to remove the items (4) and return the empty container (3), or may permit the container (3) to be taken and subsequently returned.

In some embodiments, the collection depot includes multiple docking apparatuses (54), each arranged to receive a respective transport rack (12). The computer system (2) may allocate transport racks (12) to particular docking apparatuses (54) according to available capacity, temperature requirements or collection schedules.

The docking apparatus (54) may comprise temperature-maintaining equipment, such as refrigeration, heating or ventilation means. When the transport rack (12) is docked, the docking apparatus (54) may supply conditioned air or electrical power to the rack (12) or to the containers (3), thereby maintaining the items (4) within a desired temperature range until collection.

In a preferred method, the following steps are performed:

1. receiving an order for one or more items (4) by the computer system (2);
2. assigning one or more containers (3) to the order;
3. picking the ordered items (4) at the supply depot;
4. placing the picked items (4) in the assigned container or containers (3);
5. recording, by the computer system (2), an association between the order and the container or containers (3);
6. loading the containers (3) onto a transport rack (12);
7. recording, by the computer system (2), an association between the containers (3) and the transport rack (12);
8. transporting the transport rack (12) to the collection depot;
9. docking the transport rack (12) with the docking apparatus (54);
10. making the order available for collection through the issuing station (56);
11. authenticating the customer at the issuing station (56); and
12. issuing the corresponding container (3) or items (4) to the customer.

The computer system (2) may generate notifications to the customer, for example when the order has been prepared, dispatched, arrived at the collection depot, or collected. Such notifications may be transmitted by email, SMS, push notification, automated telephone message or other electronic communication.

The system may further comprise sensors for detecting the presence or absence of containers (3) on the transport rack (12), the opening of containers (3), the temperature of items (4), the docking state of the transport rack (12), or the identity of users accessing the issuing station (56). Data from these sensors may be stored by the computer system (2) to provide an audit trail.

The invention is not limited to the embodiments described above. Features described in relation to one embodiment may be combined with features of another embodiment. The supply depot and the collection depot may be physically separate locations, or may be different areas of the same premises. The transport rack (12) may be manually movable, vehicle-mounted, autonomous, or part of a modular storage system. The issuing station (56) may be fully automated, partially automated, or operated by staff under the control of the computer system (2).

By assigning ordered items (4) to identified containers (3), arranging the containers (3) on a transport rack (12), docking the transport rack (12) at a collection depot, and issuing the items (4) through an issuing station (56), the system provides efficient and traceable delivery of ordered goods from the supply depot to the customer collection point.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert this technical concept into a patent abstract: orders are picked into containers at a warehouse, loaded onto racks according to a sequence calculated by software, moved to a pickup depot, then automatically retrieved from the rack and sent either to storage or to a service point when the consignee arrives.
counterfactuals.output: A logistics fulfillment system and method are disclosed for handling picked orders in containers. Order items are picked into respective containers at a warehouse, and software determines a loading sequence for placing the containers onto one or more transport racks. The containers are loaded onto the racks in accordance with the calculated sequence and transported to a pickup depot. At the pickup depot, an automated handling device retrieves selected containers from the racks based on order status and consignee arrival information. Retrieved containers are directed either to a storage location for later collection or to a service point for delivery to the consignee upon arrival. The system enables sequenced loading, efficient depot transfer, automated retrieval, and dynamic routing of order containers to improve pickup depot throughput and reduce manual handling.
